claim_ceiling: Metadata discovery only. These sources have not been admitted into the forest benchmark, downloaded, independently hashed, rights-cleared for a particular derivative, or ingested. Their reported scale is not a guarantee of relevant sample size for any selected task. No model calibration, forecast, thermodynamic closure, ecological conclusion or SOTA claim follows from this registry.

sources.provider: TRY Plant Trait Database / Future Earth / Max Planck Institute for Biogeochemistry / iDiv
sources.title: TRY Plant Trait Database, version 7
sources.release: Version 7 released 2026-09-04; official portal reports 22,860,407 trait records and 306,701 taxa. The About page reports approximately 23 million records, 3,260 traits, more than 7.5 million individual plants and over 100,000 measurement sites; roughly half the records are georeferenced.
observed_dimensions: leaf and wood traits where supplied
candidate_use: trait-distribution priors and sensitivity ranges for process models
trait-data representativeness and within-taxon variation audit
support_and_transfer_limits: Trait observations are not a census, biomass stock, flux, or longitudinal demographic panel.
About half the records are reported as georeferenced; do not infer site support for records without coordinates.
Version 7 taxonomic harmonization with GBIF is reported, but source-level taxon concepts and synonyms must be retained in the admission crosswalk.
A trait prior must preserve source, method, taxon, unit, sampling year and uncertainty; do not collapse distributions into a universal species constant.

rights_and_access.license_or_terms: TRY reports data from version 5.0 onward are available under CC BY with attribution, a license link and notice of changes. Verify the exact v7 extract and contributor terms before derivative or redistribution.
rights_and_access.retrieval_requirements: The portal reports delayed large data releases at times; request only the minimum required trait subset and archive the exact query/response metadata.

sources.next_gate: Select a minimal trait panel against the current process/observation variable map; retrieve exact v7 metadata and permitted extract; bind file digests, trait units, taxon concepts, measurement methods, sampling year, coordinates, quality flags and contributor conditions before use.

sources.provider: BioTIME project / University of St Andrews
sources.title: BioTIME 2.0 global biodiversity time-series database
sources.release: BioTIME 2.0 (Dornelas et al., Global Ecology and Biogeography, 2025); official database page reports 12,622,491 records, 45,073 species, 387 time series, 21 biomes and 3 realms.
candidate_use: temporal regime-shift and ecological-transfer stress tests
species/community response calibration where source sampling supports the task
support_and_transfer_limits: The database is global and multi-ecosystem, not a forest-only sample; forest subsets need an explicit biome/ecosystem and site selection rule.
Time series have different sampling protocols, taxonomic resolution, temporal cadence and observation effort; preserve the original series and metadata.
A repeated community series is not automatically an intervention dataset or causal effect estimate.
Do not random-split records from the same time series across train and test; split by independent site/series and forecast origin.

rights_and_access.license_or_terms: BioTIME 2.0 is distributed as a SQL database and CSV query under CC-BY. Each underlying study also carries its own contributor-selected licence/terms; inspect the study-level licence and attribution record before using or redistributing study-level data or derivatives. Cite the BioTIME 2.0 paper and underlying sources as required.
rights_and_access.retrieval_requirements: Retrieve the exact BioTIME 2.0 SQL/CSV release and data dictionary; preserve per-study licence identifiers, study IDs, citation metadata, site IDs, sampling effort, taxonomic crosswalk and missingness before subset selection.

sources.next_gate: Verify the exact BioTIME 2.0 data release and database-level CC-BY terms; inspect the per-study licence and contributor attribution records for every selected time series; choose forest-compatible repeated series and document site/campaign dependence, effort, taxonomy, sampling design and gaps; pre-register site-blocked and time-forward splits.

sources.provider: FLUXNET Data System / regional flux networks
sources.title: FLUXNET Data Shuttle eddy-covariance data service
sources.release: Data Shuttle GUI launched 2026-05-14. FLUXNET reports almost 6,000 site-years and a continuously updated standardized access system using ONEFlux processing; listed products include ecosystem productivity/respiration, gap filling, uncertainty and expanded metadata.
observed_dimensions: gross primary productivity and respiration products
gap-filled fluxes and uncertainty fields where supplied
candidate_use: open-system energy and carbon budget tests at compatible tower support
multi-year ecosystem response and forecast benchmarks
support_and_transfer_limits: Tower flux footprints vary with wind and stability; a tower point coordinate is not the spatial support of every interval.
Gap-filled values and measured intervals must remain distinct, including quality flags and uncertainty.
Data Shuttle site-years are heterogeneous by region, period, processing version and instrument metadata; pin product release and pipeline.
Carbon, water and energy flux availability does not by itself establish a closed first-law boundary; inspect net radiation, sensible/latent/ground heat and storage terms before closure claims.
Do not infer entropy production, exergy destruction, biological welfare or consciousness from GPP, respiration or energy flux alone.

rights_and_access.license_or_terms: FLUXNET Shuttle data are provided in alignment with FAIR/open-data policies under CC-BY, subject to FLUXNET's harmonized data-use policy. Preserve product/site DOI and required attribution; check site-specific contributor, acknowledgement and use conditions for each selected station.
rights_and_access.retrieval_requirements: Select a limited site/time slice; preserve Shuttle release/query details, ONEFlux processing/version, site metadata, quality flags, gap-fill state, uncertainty, flux-footprint metadata, station DOI and harmonized data-use acknowledgement.

sources.next_gate: Select sites with qualified carbon/water/energy terms; pin Shuttle metadata and product/site DOIs; inspect quality and gap-fill flags, footprint support, storage terms, energy-balance closure, site-level use/acknowledgement conditions and residual uncertainty before any flux or thermodynamic claim.

sources.provider: National Ecological Observatory Network (NEON) / Battelle / NSF
sources.title: NEON terrestrial organism, plant, and ecological forecast data products
sources.release: NEON RELEASE-2026 was published 2026-01-23 and includes 169 products annotated by 136 DOIs. The release notes specify Observational Systems (OS) and Airborne Observation Platform (AOP) data through 2024-12, while Instrumented Systems (IS) data extend through 2025-06. Plant phenology DP1.10055.001 RELEASE-2026 has DOI 10.48443/p75s-7p48 and its product narrative mentions observations through 2025, but the listed product date range ends 2024-12; for RELEASE-2026, treat the release manifest/product files as authoritative and keep any 2025+ records outside the release until a later stable release is pinned.

reported_coverage.measurements: plants, animals and microbes; site-level repeated sampling

observed_dimensions: species abundance, biomass/density and community composition
plant presence and cover at nested plot supports
vegetation structure and woody plant measurements
root/litterfall biomass and chemistry where collected
organismal traits and selected microbial community measures
candidate_use: plant phenology timing and abundance forecasts
independent transfer tests for plant and community process models
multi-observation tests linking organismal and ecosystem measurements
support_and_transfer_limits: NEON terrestrial sites cover the United States; this is an external transfer benchmark, not direct Amazon, Congo or New Guinea calibration.
Product-specific sampling support and cadence differ; phenology can be per individual/patch/day, while vegetation structure is plot/stem-based.

RELEASE-2026 metadata states Observational Systems and AOP through 2024-12 and Instrumented Systems through 2025-06. DP1.10055.001's RELEASE-2026 description mentions observations through 2025 while its listed date range ends 2024-12; pin files and release manifest, and do not silently treat 2025+ records as part of RELEASE-2026.
NEON data releases are fixed/citable snapshots with a DOI per product. Provisional data can be updated and are not equivalent to stable-release data; preserve release/provisional state.
NEON describes data products as free/open; downloading product data or intensive API use requires an API token. Preserve exact product DOI, data release, citation and API request metadata.
NEON4Cast evaluates forecasts by site and forecast horizon using CRPS and null-model comparisons; reproduce those scoring semantics before adding forest-specific metrics.

rights_and_access.license_or_terms: NEON publishes open data products and stable releases with product-specific DOIs. Verify the exact product/release citation and use terms, and do not mix provisional records with stable RELEASE-2026 data. Preserve the required product DOI/citation and API access terms.
rights_and_access.retrieval_requirements: Pin RELEASE-2026 and the exact product DOI and site/date query. Product downloads or intensive API use require a NEON API token. Archive query metadata, product guide, QA flags, release status and exact asset checksums.

sources.next_gate: Choose exact plant/structure/phenology products and sites; retrieve RELEASE-2026 manifest, product guides and stable files; reconcile date range against OS release cutoff 2024-12 and the phenology product's narrative; keep 2025+ observations provisional or NOT_IN_RELEASE until a later stable release is pinned; then build site-blocked/time-forward splits.
